clue.text: Writer and US president enraged university here

parts.note: Gerald Ford was the 38th President of the United States
enraged means mad, furious
Oxford is the famous English university

explanation.surface: An author and an American president, both furious, at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here' simply points to the assembled wordplay as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The English novelist of The Good Soldier and Parade's End, a writer by trade.

clue.text: Not for the first time ocean damaged net

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so these letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: to net is to gain, as in netting a profit

explanation.surface: A fishing net has been ripped by the sea yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges OCEAN into ONCEA; 'net' looks like a noun but is the verb to gain.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something again means doing it a second or later time, never the first.

clue.text: Low mark for big mouth

definitions.meaning: a ..., Greek D, is a low grade in some marking schemes
a river's ... is its wide, many-channelled mouth

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a poor examination grade, and the broad mouth where a river meets the sea.

clue.text: Advertisement more suitable for trans-formational device

parts.note: apter is the comparative of apt, meaning more suitable

explanation.surface: An advert for a gadget that is better suited to the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'trans-formational' hints at a device that converts between formats or plug types.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrical converter that lets one connector or format work with another kind.

clue.text: Dance performed by Armstrong?

definitions.meaning: a quick ballroom dance in duple time from the early twentieth century
Neil Armstrong spoke of one small stride as he set foot on the Moon

explanation.definitionFit: It names an old ballroom dance and also echoes the astronaut's famous lunar words.

clue.text: Give legal status to supporting African country's energy

parts.note: to be for something is to support it
Mali is a West African country, with its possessive S
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A move to make support for an African nation's power supply official.
explanation.definitionFit: To formalise an arrangement is to make it official, giving it legal standing.

clue.text: Part of mountain is cold place — zero Fahrenheit on top

indicators.note: zero here means none of, so that letter is dropped
on top says the dropped letter is the one at the head of the word

parts.note: a fridge is a cold place for keeping food
F is the abbreviation for the Fahrenheit temperature scale

explanation.surface: A stretch of mountain is a freezing spot, zero degrees Fahrenheit at the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zero Fahrenheit' reads as a temperature but means no F; 'on top' removes it from the front of FRIDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow crest running along the top of a mountain range.

clue.text: Head in direction of compass reading? Exactly!

parts.note: to head somewhere is to point that way
for can mean towards, as in making for home
a point is one of the 32 marked directions on a compass

explanation.surface: A navigator asks whether to steer by the compass, and gets an emphatic yes.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for in every detail, matching item by item, hence precisely.

clue.text: What a recidivist does, repeatedly

definitions.meaning: a reoffender keeps going back to prison, serving one sentence after another

explanation.definitionFit: A habitual criminal serves term upon term in jail, and the idiom also means again and again.

clue.text: Swing band with a cellist, unusually

parts.note: a band or ring is round like the letter O

indicators.note: unusually suggests the letters appear in an odd order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A swing band has, rather unusually, taken on a cellist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges A CELLIST into SCILLATE, placed after O for the ring-shaped band.
explanation.definitionFit: To oscillate is to move back and forth like a pendulum, to swing.

clue.text: Bones found in river two years after the Massacre of the Innocents?

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

parts.words: two years after the Massacre of the Innocents
parts.note: Herod's massacre happened around the birth of Christ, so two years later is AD 2, in Roman numerals AD II

explanation.surface: Bones unearthed in a river, dating from shortly after Herod's slaughter.
explanation.definitionFit: The radius is a forearm bone, and these are its plural form.

clue.text: As seen in Kenya, large antelope

indicators.note: as seen in says the letters can be spotted inside the following words

explanation.surface: A big antelope of the kind spotted on safari in Kenya.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiral-horned southern African antelope species.

clue.text: Between New Year in one country and summer in another, have food and a private meeting

indicators.note: between places the next piece in the middle of the two named pieces

parts.note: Tet is the Vietnamese New Year festival
ete is French for summer
to have food is to eat

explanation.surface: A diplomat dines privately with a counterpart somewhere between two countries' holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: French for head to head, used in English for an intimate conversation between two.

clue.text: Woman in 20s who's not staying cool?

definitions.meaning: a fashionable young woman of the 1920s jazz age
someone in a flap is flustered, losing composure

explanation.definitionFit: The jazz-age young woman, and literally one who gets into a flap and loses her cool.

clue.text: Verlaine's rhymes for ugly woman

parts.note: the poet's surname ends in a sound that two English words rhyme with, and together those words describe an unattractive woman

explanation.surface: A French poet's verses about an unattractive woman.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a dowdy, unattractive woman, both words rhyming with the poet's name.

clue.text: Each year I would take off and let go

parts.note: PA is per annum, Latin for each year
I'd is the short form of I would
taken as written

explanation.surface: Every year someone would take off and let things slide.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay someone off is to dismiss them with a final payment, letting them go.

clue.text: Head off most prejudice and social exclusion

indicators.note: head off says the first letter of the word is cut away

parts.note: racism is prejudice on grounds of race

explanation.surface: Most prejudice can be headed off, along with social exclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' looks like 'prevent' but removes the M from MOST, leaving OST.
explanation.definitionFit: Being shunned or banished from a group, as Athenians once voted to exile citizens.

clue.text: Managed to fire rifle

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
to fire someone is to sack them

explanation.surface: An armed soldier managed to fire his rifle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' looks like the gun, but is the verb to search and plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle through a place is to search it roughly and steal, to plunder it.

clue.text: King currently welcoming medical group showing expertise

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: currently means now
the WHO is the World Health Organization

explanation.surface: The monarch is now welcoming doctors who display skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Practical skill and knowledge of how to do things, informal for expertise.

clue.text: Abandoned respect for royal staff

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters are let loose into a new order

explanation.surface: Respect for the monarch's staff has been abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial rod carried by a monarch as a symbol of power.

clue.text: Release group without charge

parts.note: a set is a group of things
free means costing nothing

explanation.surface: A band of prisoners is released without being charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without charge' suggests acquittal, but means free of cost.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate or let loose, as prisoners from captivity.

clue.text: Completely mistaken, also exhausted

parts.note: a guess that is out is wrong
and adds something, meaning also
a fire that is out is spent, exhausted

explanation.surface: Someone is utterly wrong and worn out too.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning thorough or absolute, as in an out-and-out lie, hence entirely.

clue.text: Doctor's orders, having this part of the body covered

indicators.note: covered means held inside, so the letters lie within the words

explanation.surface: Doctor's instructions: keep this part of the body under wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the human body, without head or limbs.

clue.text: Animal first over threshold of ark

indicators.note: over is read as covering, one piece lying across the other

parts.note: to best someone is to come first, beating them

indicators.note: threshold means the entrance, the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: The first animal steps over the threshold of Noah's ark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' tells us BEST spans the A taken from ark.
explanation.definitionFit: A beast is any animal, especially a large four-footed one.

clue.text: Assassin of commander-in-chief and army general

definitions.meaning: John Wilkes ... shot President Lincoln, commander-in-chief of US forces
William ... founded the Salvation Army and was its first General

explanation.definitionFit: The surname of Lincoln's killer and of the Salvation Army's founding General.

clue.text: Among minor masterpieces, Bellini's work

indicators.note: among signals the letters sit inside the following words

explanation.surface: Among his lesser masterpieces is one of Bellini's works.
explanation.definitionFit: An 1831 opera by the Italian composer Vincenzo Bellini.

clue.text: Hesitant expression about member playing one instrument

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the rest

parts.note: hum, as in hum and haw, voices hesitation
an arm is a limb, a member of the body
a show that is on is playing
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Hesitantly, a band member plays a single instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A small reed organ worked by foot pedals, a keyboard instrument.

clue.text: Me and thee somehow composed old song

indicators.note: composed means put together, so these letters are assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: You and I somehow wrote an old song together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'composed' does the job, and 'and' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentimental nineteenth-century ballad by Henry Bishop, a classic old tune.
